title: Air-fryer roasted tomatoes
subtitle: Cherry tomatoes blistered and concentrated in the air fryer.
excerpt: Cherry tomatoes tossed in oil and garlic and air-fried until blistered, slightly collapsed, and intensely sweet. Ready in 15 minutes. Serves four as a side or condiment.
sourceNotes: Roasting concentrates the sugars and acids in tomatoes and reduces the water content, producing a sweeter, more intense flavour than raw tomatoes. Cherry tomatoes are well-suited to the air fryer as their size means they roast quickly and evenly.

recipe.batchNotes: Roast in batches and keep warm, or serve at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Good at room temperature and can be roasted up to 4 hours ahead.

content.text: Roasted cherry tomatoes in the air fryer are ready in 15 minutes and taste like the result of a much longer oven roast. Cook at 180°C rather than higher: too hot and the skins burst and scorch before the flesh collapses and concentrates. Leave them whole ,  halving makes them fall apart and lose their juices into the basket.

items.prepNote: left whole, on the vine if possible

content.text: Toss the {{cherry-tomatoes}} tomatoes with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, the {{garlic}} lightly crushed garlic cloves, and {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt. Preheat the air fryer to 180°C. Place in the basket ,  they can be piled up rather than in a single layer as they will shrink. Cook for 8 minutes, give the basket a gentle shake, and cook for a further 6-7 minutes until blistered and slightly collapsed. The juice from the tomatoes may collect in the drip tray ,  this is flavourful and can be poured over the tomatoes before serving.

items.fix: Cook at 180°C maximum. Gentle heat allows the skin to slowly blister rather than burst under steam pressure.

items.symptom: Skins still firm and not blistered after 15 minutes
items.cause: Air fryer not preheated, or tomatoes added cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Preheat the fryer and bring tomatoes to room temperature before cooking. Cold tomatoes need several extra minutes to start roasting.

items.cause: Tomatoes too wet or basket too crowded.
items.fix: Pat the tomatoes dry and check there is enough space for hot air to circulate. Cook in a second batch if the basket is very full.

content.text: Air-fryer roasted tomatoes work as a side with grilled meat or fish, spooned over scrambled eggs, stirred through pasta with basil and parmesan, or as a component in a salad with mozzarella and torn bread. They also keep well in a jar with olive oil for up to 3 days in the fridge.
